original_title: Exclusive U.S. Trailer for Kiyoshi Kurosawa’s Serpent’s Path Traces a Brutal Vengeance
summary_en: The master of atmospheric dread, Kiyoshi Kurosawa, is back with a chilling new vision of his own classic thriller. Prepare for a brutal journey through grief and moral decay in the just-released U.S. trailer for Serpent's Path.

en.title: Kiyoshi Kurosawa Returns to Vengeance with Haunting Serpent's Path Trailer
en.summary: The master of atmospheric dread, Kiyoshi Kurosawa, is back with a chilling new vision of his own classic thriller. Prepare for a brutal journey through grief and moral decay in the just-released U.S. trailer for Serpent's Path.
en.body:
The cinematic landscape is buzzing with anticipation as the U.S. trailer for **Kiyoshi Kurosawa**’s **Serpent's Path** has officially dropped, offering a tantalizing glimpse into a brutal tale of vengeance. This marks a significant moment for American fans of the acclaimed Japanese director, following a recent surge of his works gaining wider recognition and distribution.

## A Labyrinth of Grief and Retribution

**Serpent's Path** is a reimagining of Kurosawa's own 1998 thriller, relocating the story from Tokyo to the stark, atmospheric outskirts of Paris. The film centers on a bereaved father, portrayed by **Damien Bonnard** (known for his role in **Poor Things**), who embarks on a tortuous quest for retribution. The synopsis hints at a narrative that transcends a simple revenge story, delving into a "chilling meditation on grief, guilt, and moral decay." The trailer suggests a film steeped in Kurosawa's signature unsettling atmosphere, where the psychological toll of loss and the pursuit of justice become intertwined in a visually arresting, France-set drama.

The film boasts an impressive international cast, including **Ko Shibasaki** (who also appeared in **The Boy and the Heron**), **Hidetoshi Nishijima** (a frequent collaborator, notably in **Drive My Car**), **Mathieu Amalric**, and **Grégoire Colin**. The presence of these actors, particularly Nishijima and Amalric, alongside Kurosawa's directorial vision, promises a powerful ensemble performance that will no doubt explore the depths of human emotion.

## A Director's Creative Dialogue

For those familiar with Kurosawa's work, **Serpent's Path** might feel less like a standalone remake and more like a continuation of a thematic exploration. The original 1998 film was part of a creative period that also included **Eyes of the Spider**, a project that shared overlapping cast, crew, and even premise. Kurosawa himself has indicated that he views **Serpent's Path** as being "more in his creative spirit" than a strict remake, suggesting an evolution of ideas and a deeper engagement with his own cinematic language. This new iteration, set against the backdrop of Paris, allows Kurosawa to engage with his own "fish-out-of-water" experience in France, adding another layer of meta-commentary to the unfolding narrative.

## What's Next

**Serpent's Path** is set to open in the U.S. on September 11th, distributed by KimStim. With the release of the U.S. trailer, anticipation is high for this haunting exploration of vengeance, grief, and the moral complexities that lie within us all.

tr.title: Kiyoshi Kurosawa İntikamla Geri Döndü: Haunting Serpent's Path Fragmanı
tr.summary: Atmosferik dehşetin ustası Kiyoshi Kurosawa, yeni bir vizyonla geri döndü. Serpent's Path'un ABD fragmanının yayınlanmasıyla, intikam ve ahlaki çöküntü konusunda bizi zorlu bir yolculuğa çıkarıyor.
tr.body:
Sinema dünyası, Kiyoshi Kurosawa'nın yeni filmi Serpent's Path'un ABD fragmanının yayınlanmasıyla heyecan içinde. Bu, Kurosawa'nın çalışmalarının son dönemde daha geniş bir kitle tarafından tanınması ve dağıtılmasıyla birlikte, ABD'li hayranları için önemli bir an. 

## Acı ve İntikam Labirenti
Serpent's Path, Kurosawa'nın 1998 tarihli aynı adlı gerilim filminin yeniden hayal edilmiş hali. Film, Tokyo'dan Paris'in atmosferik dış mahallelerine taşınan bir hikayeyi anlatıyor. Damien Bonnard'ın canlandırdığı bir babanın intikam arayışını konu alıyor. Senaryo, basit bir intikam hikayesinin ötesine geçerek, acı, suçluluk ve ahlaki çöküntü üzerine etkileyici bir meditasyona dönüşüyor. Fragman, Kurosawa'nın imzası taşıyan rahatsız edici atmosferin hakim olduğu, psikolojik gerilim ve dramın iç içe geçtiği bir film vaat ediyor.

Filmin uluslararası kadrosunda Ko Shibasaki, Hidetoshi Nishijima, Mathieu Amalric ve Grégoire Colin gibi önemli isimler yer alıyor. Özellikle Nishijima ve Amalric'in varlığı, Kurosawa'nın vizyonuyla birlikte güçlü bir performans vaat ediyor. 

## Yönetmenin Sanatsal Diyalogu
Kurosawa'nın önceki çalışmalarını tanıyanlar için Serpent's Path, bağımsız bir yeniden yapım değil, daha çok tematik bir araştırmanın devamı gibi hissedebilir. Aslında, 1998 tarihli orijinal film, aynı dönemde çekilen Eyes of the Spider ile benzer bir creative dönem içinde yer alıyordu. Kurosawa, Serpent's Path'i bir yeniden yapım olarak değil, kendi yaratıcı ruhunun daha derin bir ifadesi olarak görüyor. Bu, fikirlerin evrimi ve kendi sinemasal dilinin daha da gelişmesi anlamına geliyor. Paris'in atmosferinde geçen bu yeni versiyon, Kurosawa'nın kendi 'yabancı' deneyimini yansıtıyor ve anlatıya meta-açıklamalar katıyor.

## Sonraki Adımlar
Serpent's Path, 11 Eylül'de KimStim tarafından dağıtılacak. ABD fragmanının yayınlanmasıyla birlikte, intikam, acı ve ahlaki karmaşıklikler üzerine bu etkileyici keşif için beklenti yüksek.

content_raw: There has never been a better time for American Kiyoshi Kurosawa fans. The recent run of restorations and new work hits a high point with today’s U.S. release of his excellent The Samurai and the Prisoner , tomorrow’s ultra-rare 35mm screening of Charisma , and the latter’s pending release from Janus Films (acquired alongside his marvelous Eyes of the Spider ). Next month will finally bring the stateside debut of Serpent’s Path , a France-set remake of 1998’s feel-bad triumph that stars Damien Bonnard ( Poor Things ), Ko Shibasaki ( The Boy and the Heron ), Hidetoshi Nishijima ( Drive My Car , Her Private Hell ), Mathieu Amalric, and Claire Denis regular Grégoire Colin. Ahead of a September 11 opening from KimStim, we’re thrilled to premiere the trailer. Those who know the original will be familiar with this iteration’s premise, then all the more surprised by its eventual turns—not least some reflection on the director’s own fish-out-of-water position in France. As the first go-round was complemented by the aforementioned  Eyes —a project made with overlapping cast, crew, and premise—it sometimes seems  Serpent’s Path  is less a remake than the third in a series. (Kurosawa at least  told me  he considers it more in his creative spirit.) But I’ll let you see the movie and decide for yourself. Here’s the official synopsis: “Kiyoshi Kurosawa revisits and reimagines his own 1998 thriller in this haunting French-language adaptation of Serpent’s Path , transforming a revenge story into a chilling meditation on grief, guilt, and moral decay. Relocating the action from Tokyo to the bleak outskirts of Paris, the film follows a bereaved father (Damien Bonnard) who embarks on a labyrinthine quest for vengeance against a shadowy child-trafficking organization known as ‘The Circle,’ aided by the enigmatic and unnervingly composed Sayoko, played with hypnotic ambiguity by Ko Shibasaki. Expanding upon the original’s psychological terrain while retaining its eerie inevitability, Kurosawa crafts a masterclass in atmosphere and existential dread, proving once again why he remains one of cinema’s great architects of unease.” Find the preview below: The post Exclusive U.S. Trailer for Kiyoshi Kurosawa’s Serpent’s Path Traces a Brutal Vengeance first appeared on The Film Stage .
